Accused No.1 in Crime No.211/2023 registered by Chowk Police Station, Kalaburagi City for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 302, 304B R/w 34 of IPC is before this Court seeking regular bail.

2. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.
3. FIR in Crime No.211/2023 was registered by Chowk Police Station, Kalaburagi City for the aforesaid offences against the petitioner and his married sister.

During the course of investigation,
the petitioner was arrested on 01.11.2023.
Investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed.
The bail NC: 2024:KHC-K:3843 application filed by the petitioner under Section 439 of Cr.P.C, before the Trial Court in Crl.Misc.No.508/2024 was dismissed on 15.04.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition submits that the petitioner has two minor children who are required to be taken care of.
He submits that on perusal of material available on record, it is very clear that the death of the petitioner's wife was due to suicide.
However, false allegation has been made against the petitioner and his sister.
He submits that the petitioner who has no criminal antecedents is in custody from 01.11.2023.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader has opposed the bail petition.
She submits that the marriage of the deceased with the petitioner had taken place in the year 2020.

The death has occurred in the year 2023 and therefore there is a presumption as against the NC:
2024:KHC-K:3843 petitioner in law.
She accordingly, prays to dismiss the petition.

6. The material on record would go to show that on the basis of typed first information dated 31.10.2023 submitted by the first informant Rajendr who is the father of the deceased Ratnabai, FIR was registered in Crime No.211/2023 against the petitioner and his sister.

In the first information it is averred that the marriage of the petitioner with Ratnabai was solemnized in the year 2020 and from the said wedlock, they have two children aged about 3 years and 1 year respectively.
7.
On 31.10.2023 at about 6.00 a.m, the petitioner had allegedly telephoned first informant and informed him that Ratnabai was not well and therefore he has taking her to the hospital.
Ten minutes thereafter, he had once again telephoned first informant and informed him that Ratnabai had died.
The first informant thereafter went to the house of the petitioner and found his daughter dead.
The first informant suspected foul play in the death NC: 2024:KHC-K:3843 of his daughter.
It is in this background, he had approached the police and submitted his first information, based on which FIR in Crime No.211/2023 was registered.

8. As per averments made in the first information dated 31.10.2023 at about 6.00 a.m, itself the petitioner had telephoned the first informant and inform him that Ratnabai was not well and therefore, she was taken to the hospital.
The allegation against the petitioner and his married sister is that at about 6.00 a.m, on 31.10.2023 they have strangulated Ratnabai to death by using a saree.
9. The postmortem report of deceased Ratnabai would go to show that thyroid bone and thyroid cartilage were intact.

After investigation, the police have filed charge sheet only for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 302 & 304B R/w 34 of IPC and no charge sheet is filed for the offence punishable under the provisions of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The petitioner who has no other criminal antecedent is in custody from NC: 2024:KHC-K:3843 01.11.2023.
Accused No.2 has been already enlarged on bail by the jurisdictional Sessions Court.
Under the circumstances, I am of the view that the petitioner has made out a prima-facie case for grant of regular bail.
10. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
